activities.anchor: The same functional-group alphabet (11.1) organises all of biology
activities.caption: pair each handle with the job biology grips it for
activities.name: bioHandleMatch

config.prompt: Six handles do nearly all the work — pair each with its job:

pairs.right: the chemistry of metabolism's middle steps
fatty and amino acids' acid character
energy's handle — ATP, DNA's backbone, the signalling switch
cysteines weld proteins with disulfide bridges

config.why: Each handle has its characteristic reactions, and biochemistry is those reactions selected, catalysed and sequenced — with the phosphate family as the Goldilocks currency at about 30 kJ/mol.

activities.anchor: Nomenclature (11.2) in biology compresses structure into family names
activities.caption: file each fact by biomolecule family
activities.name: bioFamilyBuckets

config.prompt: Four families, one logic. File each fact:

items.label: glucose C₆H₁₂O₆, named by its aldehyde position
D-sugars almost exclusively — handedness as a fossil choice
twenty kinds, written Gly, Ala, Leu… so sequences become text
an amino group, a carboxyl group and a side chain on one carbon
palmitic acid C16:0 — the numbers are the recipe
oleic acid C18:1 — chain length and unsaturation

config.why: 'The protein is 153 amino acids starting Met-Gly…' is a molecular structure precise enough to synthesise — vocabulary as compression.

config.prompt: Burning glucose outright releases about how many kilojoules per mole as heat?
config.why: About 2,800 kJ/mol — respiration releases the same total in installments the cell can bank, at roughly a third capture efficiency; the remainder is the heat that keeps you warm.
config.context: The four stages: glycolysis in the cytoplasm, the Krebs cycle and electron transport in the mitochondria.

activities.anchor: Energy density follows from reduction state
activities.caption: drag the divider — the two fuel stores
activities.name: bioFuelCompare

config.prompt: Fat vs sugar as fuel — drag the divider:

before.label: fat (palmitate)
before.text: Nine kilocalories per gram; complete oxidation yields about 106 ATP — reduced hydrocarbon chains carry more electrons per carbon. The stock for storage; membranes are its inert fabric.

after.label: sugar (glucose)
after.text: Four kilocalories per gram; roughly 30 ATP per glucose. Glycogen is only for sprint — but it mobilises fast and works without oxygen.

config.why: Muscle, brain and fuel-choice are combustion economics: gram for gram, fat stores about two and a half times more.

activities.anchor: Two hydroxyls on adjacent carbons can join through an
activities.caption: true or false — one toggle, opposite materials
activities.name: bioSugarJudge

statements.s: Starch is α-linked glucose — digestible and spiral.
statements.why: The glycosidic bond's stereochemistry is the toggle.

statements.s: Cellulose is β-linked glucose — indigestible to us, straight, and the world's most abundant organic compound.
statements.why: Wood: cows digest it with bacterial help; termites outsource to gut symbionts.

statements.s: Cellulose is easily digested by humans because it is just glucose, like starch.
statements.why: Same monomer, opposite link — the β-bond is the whole difference.

statements.s: Fermentation regenerates NAD⁺ so glycolysis can keep running without oxygen.
statements.why: Yeasts end at ethanol; your muscles end one step earlier at lactate — the burn of sprint metabolising.

activities.anchor: The Krebs cycle is a rotating cast of tricarboxylic and dicarboxylic acids
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the acid bookkeeping
activities.name: bioKrebsCloze

config.text: The Krebs cycle is a rotating cast of tri- and dicarboxylic acids — %%0%% (three carboxyls), succinate, fumarate, malate, oxaloacetate. Your blood's pH is buffered within %%1%% of 7.4, outside which enzymes begin to denature.
config.hint: The cycle's namesake is the three-carboxyl member; the buffer holds pH to a hundredth-scale tolerance.

activities.anchor: double helix 3 billion base pairs long
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the information polymer
activities.name: bioDnaEstimate

config.prompt: Human DNA is a double helix of roughly how many base pairs, packed into each cell nucleus?
config.why: About 3 billion — some 2 metres of it per nucleus, joined by phosphodiester links (a double condensation per bond), the four-letter alphabet as chemistry's highest-information polymer.
config.context: Insulin is 51 residues; haemoglobin 574 — sequence-encoded chains that fold into machines.

activities.anchor: unchanged by the reaction, reused thousands of times a second
activities.caption: one line of the enzyme summary is wrong
activities.name: bioEnzymeSpot

config.prompt: One line of this enzyme summary is wrong. Find it.
lines: Enzymes are proteins — catalysts, unchanged by the reactions they catalyse
They are reused thousands of times a second until they denature
They are alive, and they reproduce inside the cell
What is special is their shape
Denaturation is unfolding — boiled egg: chemistry intact, function gone
config.correction: Enzymes are not alive, cannot reproduce, and obey ordinary chemistry.
config.why: Shape is the special thing — which is why heat or wrong pH kills an enzyme by unfolding it while leaving the amino acid sequence untouched, and why most drugs are simply enzyme grips, occupied.
